claims.text: A physics-informed machine-learning model using hierarchical-microstructure descriptors can predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior in HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed model will be faster and more accurate than conventional DFT/MD simulations.
As-fabricated HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure containing nanoscale precipitates, grain boundaries, and interfacial regions.
The predictive framework will combine machine-learning feature selection based on hierarchical-microstructure descriptors with streamlined atomistic calculations.
The hypothesis applies to quasi-static tensile and fracture testing at room temperature.
At low to moderate strain rates, the hierarchical heterostructure governs the deformation response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Hierarchical interfaces and nanoscale precipitates redistribute local stress.
Hierarchical interfaces and nanoscale precipitates control dislocation mobility.
Hierarchical interfaces and nanoscale precipitates impede fracture propagation.
Elastic properties, interfacial or surface energies, and misfit volumes are physically relevant descriptors for models of alloy strength and ductility.
These descriptors allow the model to capture stress transfer and dislocation interactions that dominate the elastic and fracture response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Targeted feature integration reduces computational expense while preserving the critical physical information needed for prediction.
The proposed model will reduce simulation time by approximately 50–70%.
The proposed model will produce errors for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture parameters that are 10–20% lower than errors from conventional DFT/MD simulations.
Direct DFT treatment of alloy yield and fracture is computationally challenging and often beyond available implementations.
Established DFT/MD simulations inadequately resolve heterostructural effects and consequently have higher predictive variability.
The model may fail at extreme strain rates, elevated temperatures, or when relevant long-range interactions are absent from its descriptors or training data.
Calibration data specific to HfNbTiVAl10 are limited.
Independent measurements will include elastic-slope Young’s modulus, 0.2%-offset yield strength, and standardized fracture-related measurements.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if prediction deviations exceed 30% or computational-time savings relative to DFT/MD are below 20%.
